question.text: An inclined plane is bent in such a way that the vertical cross-section is given by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math> where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi></math> is in vertical and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> in horizontal direction. If the upper surface of this curved plane is rough with coefficient of friction <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>μ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo></math> the maximum height in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi></math> at which a stationary block will not slip downward is________<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi><mo>.</mo></math>

solution.text:
At maximum ht. block will experience maximum friction force. Therefore if at this height slope of the tangent is tanθ, then θ=Angle of repose

∴  tanθ=dydx=2x4=x2=0.5

⇒x=1 and therefore y=x24=0.25 m

=25 cm

∴ Answer is 25 cm

(Assuming that x & y in the equation are given in meter)
